metadata.note: The Milwaukee Road's Pacific Coast Extension, Aberdeen S.D. to Seattle and Tacoma, completed 14 May 1909 and carrying passengers until the Olympian Hiawatha was discontinued on 22 May 1961. The repo previously drew the Milwaukee Road only as far west as Aberdeen (data/milwaukee_road_chicago_aberdeen.geojson); the research report calls this absence 'the single biggest gap' on the railroad. Five features, about 1,497 route miles, built from research/branches/chicago_milwaukee_st_paul_and_pacific_railroad.txt blocks [6] through [11]. THE 1980 TRAP: the Milwaukee abandoned the Extension west of Miles City in 1980, and the electrification came down in 1972 (Coast) and June 1974 (Rocky Mountain). None of those is a passenger date and none of them appears as a year here. The named trains - the Olympian (1911-1947), the Olympian Hiawatha (1947-1961) and The Columbian - ran over these same five features and are described in the segment notes rather than drawn as separate lines.
metadata.source: Official Guide of the Railways, February 1952 (schedules effective 30 September 1951), Table 1, full OCR at research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt; research/branches/chicago_milwaukee_st_paul_and_pacific_railroad.txt; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Road_electrification
not_yet_sourced: The alignment between Plummer Junction and Marengo. The Feb 1952 Guide's Table 1 runs the through trains via Spokane and Cheney, which is NOT the Milwaukee's own Palouse main line (Tekoa - Rosalia - Malden - Ewan, 10-27 km to the south). About 79 miles of the Avery - Spokane - Othello feature therefore runs on OSM ways tagged Union Pacific. The Milwaukee is understood to have reached Spokane over foreign track, but no source for that arrangement was checked in this pass. Someone with a Milwaukee Road employee timetable or a valuation map could settle it in minutes.

The Milwaukee's own Palouse main line, Plummer Junction - Malden - Marengo (report block [65], drawable 1910-1925, an end that is a floor rather than a finding) is NOT drawn here. OSM carries it well - it is the Palouse to Cascades trail east of Ewan - so it is a cheap addition for a later pass.
Ismay - Miles City, Mont., 51.5 mi: OSM has no rail on this part of the abandoned grade, so it is drawn as a straight line. It is the only ruled leg in the file.

The 1961-1964 end of trains 15/16 (Minneapolis - Deer Lodge) is the research report's figure and was not independently verified. The Harlowton - Deer Lodge portion is drawn to 1961 rather than 1964, understating those miles by three years.
Every avg_speed_kmh here is one figure derived from the advertised 45-hour Chicago - Puget Sound schedule and applied to all five legs. No leg has its own timed speed.
branches_deliberately_omitted: The Spokane - Newport - Metaline Falls line (report block [75], drawable 1909-1923), the Grays Harbor, Mount Rainier, Olympic Peninsula, Bellingham and Moses Lake branches (blocks [66]-[69], [76]-[81]) and the Palouse line (block [65]) are all left for a later pass; this file is the through route only.

properties.company: Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul and Pacific Railroad
properties.line: Milwaukee Road: Aberdeen – Miles City – Harlowton
properties.speed_source: end-to-end average, not a track speed: the Feb 1952 Guide advertises the Olympian Hiawatha at 'only 45 hours Chicago to Puget Sound' over the 2,188-mile route, which is 48.6 mph / 78 km/h including every stop. Applied to each leg of the through route; the leg-by-leg figure is NOT separately sourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror), 2026-08-30: all railway ways in the corridor, weighted by old_railway_operator (Milwaukee 1.0, untagged 3.0, another named operator 40.0) plus the rail-trails built on the abandoned grade, routed waypoint to waypoint with a corridor-masked Dijkstra over 8 snap candidates per waypoint chosen by dynamic programming.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 601.9 mi against the report's documented ~570 mi for Aberdeen - Harlowton (+6%). Every one of the fifteen named waypoints lies within 1.2 km of the drawn line. ONE APPROXIMATED LEG: Ismay - Miles City, 51.5 mi (9% of the feature), drawn as a straight line because OSM carries no rail of any kind on that part of the abandoned grade - the only railway in the window is the ex-Northern Pacific BNSF Forsyth Subdivision along the Yellowstone, which is a different railroad and was deliberately not used. A further 1.3 mi is short bridges across breaks in the OSM ways. East of Miles City the route runs over today's BNSF Mobridge and Hettinger Subdivisions (308 mi) and over ways OSM names 'Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul and Pacific Railroad' (175 mi): the BNSF subdivisions occupy the Milwaukee's own alignment and were taken over after the 1980 retrenchment, but OSM carries no old_railway_operator tag on them, so that identification rests on the station sequence and mileage matching the Guide, not on a tag. ALIGNMENT ERA: this is the surviving/abandoned alignment as mapped today, which for this line is the 1909 alignment; no later realignment is known on it.

segments.note: Prairie section of the Pacific Coast Extension, opened with the through route 14 May 1909: Aberdeen - Mobridge - Lemmon - Hettinger - Bowman - Marmarth - Baker - Miles City - Melstone - Roundup - Harlowton. Carried the Olympian (from 28 May 1911), the Olympian Hiawatha (from 29 June 1947) and The Columbian. Marmarth N.D. and Miles City appear in the Feb 1952 Guide's Table 1 with real times, so 1951 service is directly confirmed. Headway 720 min = the two daily through trains each way the Guide itself advertises: 'THE MILWAUKEE ROAD offers double daily service -- the Diesel and electrically operated Olympian Hiawatha and The Columbian.' That is a counted frequency, not an estimate. *** The Milwaukee Road abandoned the Pacific Extension west of Miles City in 1980; that is a FREIGHT event nineteen years after the last passenger train and is deliberately absent from these years.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 439.5 mi against the documented 438 route miles under wire (Harlowton - Avery) - a 0% difference, the best fit of the five legs. No straight-line approximation at all; 7.6 mi is short bridges across breaks between OSM ways, the longest of them in the abandoned Butte - Deer Lodge section. 360 mi of the route runs on ways OSM names as the Milwaukee Road grade ('Ex Milwaukee Road ROW', 'Old Milwaukee Road', 'Abandoned Milwaukee Road Railroad', 'Route of the Olympian', 'Route of the Hiawatha Trail'). segments.note: The Rocky Mountain Division: Harlowton - Martinsdale - Ringling - Three Forks - Butte (over Pipestone Pass) - Deer Lodge - Drummond - Missoula - Alberton - St. Regis - Avery (through the St. Paul Pass tunnel). Steam from 1909; electrified at 3,000 V DC in stages in 1915-1916 - the first long-distance mainline electrification in the United States, worked by bipolars and later the Little Joes, with regenerative braking down the Continental Divide. Butte and Deer Lodge are in the Feb 1952 Guide's Table 1. Headway 720 min = the two daily through trains each way the Guide itself advertises: 'THE MILWAUKEE ROAD offers double daily service -- the Diesel and electrically operated Olympian Hiawatha and The Columbian.' That is a counted frequency, not an estimate. *** The catenary came down in June 1974 and the track in 1980. NEITHER is a passenger date: the last passenger train over the whole division was 22 May 1961, and trains 15/16 ran only as far west as Deer Lodge to 1964. This feature follows report block [7]'s drawable of 1909-1961 rather than extending the Harlowton - Deer Lodge portion to 1964; that understates those 225 miles by three years and is deliberate, not a finding that service there stopped in 1961.

No straight-line approximation. All nine waypoints lie within 1.4 km of the drawn line. *** COMPANY-OF-TRACK CAVEAT, the important one on this feature: only 125.9 mi runs on ways OSM tags as the Milwaukee Road. About 79 mi - Spokane, Cheney and on south-west towards Marengo - runs on ways OSM tags Union Pacific, and 16 mi on BNSF-named ways. That is not obviously an error: the Milwaukee's OWN main line across the Palouse ran well to the south through Tekoa, Rosalia, Malden and Ewan (10-27 km away, and by 1951 printed in the Guide as a separate local table), while the through trains ran via Spokane, which is what Table 1 prints. The Milwaukee is understood to have reached Spokane over another company's rails, but THAT ARRANGEMENT WAS NOT SOURCED in this pass, so the drawn alignment between Plummer Junction and Marengo should be treated as unverified. The company's own Palouse main line (report block [65], drawable 1910-1925) is NOT drawn.

segments.note: Idaho Division and the through route across eastern Washington: Avery - Calder - St. Maries - Plummer Junction - Spokane - Cheney - Marengo - Ralston - Lind - Warden - Othello. This is the station order the Feb 1952 Guide's Table 1 actually prints, read off the through-train column. Avery - Othello was the unelectrified gap between the Rocky Mountain and Coast Divisions and was steam and then diesel throughout. Spokane was the Olympian Hiawatha's largest intermediate stop west of Butte. Headway 720 min = the two daily through trains each way the Guide itself advertises: 'THE MILWAUKEE ROAD offers double daily service -- the Diesel and electrically operated Olympian Hiawatha and The Columbian.' That is a counted frequency, not an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 189.2 mi Othello - Seattle, against the documented 207 route miles Othello - Tacoma (a different pair of endpoints: adding this feature's Seattle - Tacoma neighbour brings the comparable figure to about 211 mi, a 2% difference). No straight-line approximation; 4.6 mi is short bridges across breaks in the OSM ways, the largest a 1.4 km break in the rail-trail west of Kittitas. 178.6 mi of the route - 94% - runs on the Milwaukee's own grade, most of it now the Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail and the Cedar River Trail, which are the abandoned right of way itself and are used here as real geometry rather than a ruled line. Only 7.5 mi runs on BNSF-named ways, in the Seattle terminal area. ALIGNMENT ERA: the trail follows the 1909/1915 alignment, including the Beverly bridge and the Boylston and Snoqualmie tunnels, so the drawn geometry is of the feature's own era.

segments.note: The Coast Division: Othello - Beverly (over the Columbia) - Kittitas - Cle Elum - Hyak and the 2.3-mile Snoqualmie Tunnel - Cedar Falls - Maple Valley - Renton - Seattle. Steam from 1909, electrified at 3,000 V DC 1917-1920; with the Rocky Mountain Division's 438 these 207 miles make up the Milwaukee's famous 656 electrified miles. Tacoma and North Puyallup are printed with real times in the Feb 1952 Guide's Table 1. Headway 720 min = the two daily through trains each way the Guide itself advertises: 'THE MILWAUKEE ROAD offers double daily service -- the Diesel and electrically operated Olympian Hiawatha and The Columbian.' That is a counted frequency, not an estimate. *** De-electrified 1972 and the grade is now the Palouse to Cascades trail; neither is a passenger date. The last passenger train was 22 May 1961.
